rationale: Round 4, ADR-conformance lens. I read a593792a fresh from disk, along with reattest.go and the executor binding writer at that commit; this was read-only. My three round-3 asks are ADDRESSED or moot, except a date gap on the staged skill line (PARTIAL). The finder-only fallback is the right ADR-0041 posture: no automatic path accepts an undirected `Merge bead/<id>`, MF-3 fails loud and names the candidate, and acceptance needs operator-vouched audited reattest with exactly one candidate. That withdraws the round-3 tie-break departure from FIX-2b and Spec-125. The binding veto and audited repair are unchanged and sound. Scoping the unreached-review refusal to fallback candidates is correct; a global version would refuse every primary-path reattest after a rebased-away round. But the spec's own premise ('a rebased-away review round is normal') holds on the fallback path too, and the new ReattestStateUnlandedReview names no forward exit. MF-3's only recovery for a fallback candidate is `mindspec reattest`, so a genuine #239-shape landing whose bead also had a rebased-away round dead-ends: MF-3 recommends reattest, and reattest refuses permanently. That is the ADR-0041 §2(i) defect in miniature, and it is why I request changes; the fix is one recovery line and one AC leg. On the forge question: the reattest-audited read-back adds no forge resistance (the audit keys are as agent-writable as the binding), which the spec states honestly and which matches ADR-0037 §8 and Spec-125. However, it is vulnerable to NON-malicious staleness. The executor's binding write goes through bead.MergeMetadata and does not clear the earlier mindspec_landed_reattest_* keys. The read-back test ('binding names that SHA and an audit record with this scanned branch exists') does not bind the audit to the binding values, so a later executor-written binding can inherit an old reattest audit and pass as reattest-accepted.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 (ii) ReattestStateUnlandedReview: name an ADR-0041 §2(i) forward exit, and pin it in AC-11 (vii)/(viii)/(ix). The spec's own reason for scoping ('a rebased-away review round is normal') applies on the fallback path too, so a real #239-shape landing whose bead had a rebased-away round refuses permanently while MF-3 keeps recommending `mindspec reattest`. The refusal's recovery should name the audited exits that remain: for the dependent, `mindspec next <dependent> --allow-not-ready=MF-3 --evidence <path-to-justification>`, and/or the ADR-0035 mindspec-q9ea attested-restore. MF-3's off-first-parent message should list that second exit too, after reattest.

R4.2 read-back: bind the reattest audit to the binding it vouches for. Today `reattest.go` writes the audit keys (actor, at, op, corroboration, prior pair, scanned_branch) but no 'accepted merge SHA / second parent' key. The executor's merge-time binding write goes through `bead.MergeMetadata` and leaves earlier `mindspec_landed_reattest_*` keys in place. As written ('binding names that merge … AND carries a reattest audit record whose scanned branch is this spec branch'), a later executor-written binding can therefore inherit a stale audit from an earlier reattest. Add a fix: either reattest records `mindspec_landed_reattest_merge_sha`/`…_second_parent`, which must equal the binding for the read-back to accept, or the executor's binding write clears the reattest audit keys. Add an AC leg: an executor binding written over an older reattest audit does not confirm a fallback candidate.

R4.2 read-back: apply R6.3's validity discipline to the audit record that grants acceptance. It is VALID only when `at` is RFC-3339, `op` is reattest's op constant, actor is non-empty, scanned_branch equals the spec branch, and the new SHA keys match the binding. Anything else is MALFORMED and does not confirm. This raises no forge bar (the residual is stated); it stops accidental partial writes from passing.

R6.5 staged line vs ADR-0045 Decision 5: the transition clause defers only the `doctor` DATE CHECK to the rule table. The MARKING duty ('must show the ID of its target gate or config key, and a removal date') applies now to a rule staged after acceptance. Either put a provisional removal date in the SKILL.md marker now (the rule table can revise it), or amend the Decision 5 transition sentence to say a pre-rule-table staged rule shows its target and records its date in the rule table when step 1 lands. Extend AC-18 to pin the staged marker (target `next-action`, spec 133) in SKILL.md itself, not only the ready-check line.

findings.title: Round-3 ask status
findings.detail: Re-derived at a593792a. r3.1 (fallback tie-break departs from FIX-2b / Spec-125) ADDRESSED, by being made moot: Ruling 1 withdraws the tie-break, reattest requires exactly one owned candidate with no grouping, and touchpoint (i)'s 'Earlier rules superseded' bullet records the departure and its withdrawal. r3.2 ('executor writes it only' is false) ADDRESSED: the sentence is gone, the binding is described as agent-writable and written by both the executor and reattest, and only a reattest-audited binding confirms a fallback candidate. That raises the new staleness gap in ask 2. r3.3 (new ms-bead-impl line vs ADR-0045 Decision 4/5) PARTIAL: it is now marked as a staged rule with target `next-action` (spec 133), but no removal date is shown, and the transition clause defers only the doctor date check, not the marking duty (ask 4).

findings.title: Restated ADR-0041 amendment (finder-only) — judged
findings.detail: Touchpoint (i) now says: FIND and NAME only; no automatic acceptance; a typed `*LandedMergeOffFirstParent` that wraps ErrLandedMergeNotFound and never ErrLandedMergeNoCandidate, so R4.4's 'only the zero-candidate arm may say no landing exists' is preserved; acceptance only by audited reattest with exactly one candidate; CLOSE paths first-parent only. This is the most conservative reading of §2(ii) 'never subject text alone', and it removes all three round-2/3 automatic false PASSes by construction rather than by enumerating corroborations. The binding veto (ii) and fourth-verb (iii) bullets are unchanged and sound. AC-18 enumerates every element for the text-pin.

findings.title: Fallback-scoped UnlandedReview refusal has no named forward exit (ADR-0041 §2(i))
findings.detail: Scoping is correct: globally, every primary-path reattest after a rebased-away or force-reset review round would refuse, and MF-3 NoEvidence's recovery is reattest, so that would deadlock. But the same normal event (a rebased-away round SHA in panel.json) can coexist with a genuine off-first-parent landing. Then MF-3 → off-first-parent → `mindspec reattest` → ReattestStateUnlandedReview, and nothing in R4.2 or AC-11 names what the operator does next. ADR-0041 §2(i): 'Every refusal's named recovery MUST be a step that can actually change the fact being refused on.' Deleting the panel registration would be the only implicit exit, and that destroys review evidence. The audited forward exits do exist (R6's scoped MF-3 override with evidence; the q9ea attested-restore) and should be named.

findings.title: Reattest-audited read-back can inherit a stale audit (not forge, staleness)
findings.detail: At a593792a, reattest.go writes the binding SHAs plus mindspec_landed_reattest_{actor,at,op,corroboration,prior_merge_sha,prior_second_parent,scanned_branch} in one MergeMetadata call. No audit key records which merge was accepted, apart from free text inside `corroboration`. The executor's merge-time binding write uses bead.MergeMetadata (mindspec_executor.go mergeBindingFn), which merges and so leaves old reattest_* keys behind. The R4.2 read-back condition does not tie the audit to the current binding values. On forgery: the audit adds no forge resistance over the binding itself, the spec says so, and that is consistent with ADR-0037 §8 and the Spec-125 amendment's 'detectable-by-inspection, NOT cryptographically tamper-proof'. No objection there.

findings.title: Staged ms-bead-impl line: target shown, date deferred beyond what the transition clause allows
findings.detail: ADR-0045 Decision 5 (as amended at 4c46cf64): 'this marking duty applies to a rule that is staged in a skill after this ADR is accepted ... The doctor date check starts when the rule table (step 1) exists'. R6.5 assigns the removal date 'in the rule table when step 1 lands', so the skill line carries no date when it is written. Either the ADR text or the spec must move. AC-18 also pins only the ready-check exit-code line, not the staged marker.

findings.title: Membership/N4 — ADR-lens only
findings.detail: Plan-form ID + FindEpicForBead lineage + MF-1 plan.md mapping is a stricter, tracker-plus-repo predicate. It aligns selection with readiness's own MF-1 source, so ADR-0041's fourth-verb preflight evaluates the same bead it dispatches. N4 (unmapped plan-form follow-ups) is informational and changes no exit code, so it is consistent with the ADR-0035 HC-4 statement in the touchpoints. No ADR conflict found. Deeper attacks on N4 are for F3/G3.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: (1) Header lines 11–12 still say to write '<your-slot>-round-4.json beside this BRIEF'. The 'Verdict location (overrides the header)' section corrects it, but the contradiction stays in the machine header. (2) Fixed since round 3: the Summary no longer cites `git show 7a490064` and now says 'at the reviewed commit in the header'. (3) The Round-4 section calls the global unreached-review refusal a §2(i) deadlock 'after a rebased-away round'. That is right, but the BRIEF does not ask whether the fallback-scoped refusal needs its own forward exit, and it does (see major finding). No other errors found on disk.
